questionText: What is the Spring Boot property hierarchy and what takes highest precedence?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can predict the winner among common runtime property sources and explain why command line is not the unconditional top source in every test or servlet context.

claims.statement: Within common runtime deployment inputs, Spring Boot gives command-line arguments higher priority than Java system properties, which outrank OS environment variables and application config data.
Inside Spring Boot config data, profile-specific files override non-profile files and external files can override equivalent files packaged inside the application.
Spring Boot's complete order also contains test, JSON, servlet, JNDI, and other sources, including test-specific settings that can have higher priority than command-line arguments.

examples.title: Verify the exact four-source server.port precedence example

validation.command: Run the Java 17 Spring Boot 3.3.1 fixture with file value 8080, SERVER_PORT=9090, system property 6060, and command-line value 7070
validation.expected: ConfigurableEnvironment returns 7070 as the effective server.port

visuals.title: Common runtime sources ordered from higher to lower priority

notes: The table explicitly labels itself as a common subset so it does not falsely make command line the absolute highest source.

review.notes: The complete source order and config-data sub-order were checked against Spring Boot 3.3.1; the exact file/environment/system/command-line winner was verified in an integration test.
